_doc: One row per exit that removes an issue from a RUN OF A REGISTERED DRIVER.
THREE DRIVERS, ONE REGISTRY (ASK-353). v1 declared a single `source`,
linear-worker.sh, and reported green while converge.sh and kipi-dispatch.sh
dead-ended freely -- two of the three code paths that can strand an issue were
never walked. Per-driver registries drift, so `sources` is a list and every row
names the source it belongs to. A marker is matched only inside its own source.
IDENTITY IS A STABLE MARKER, NEVER A LINE NUMBER (finding-15). The PRD's own
v1 cited linear-worker.sh:1297 (which resets variables), :1295 (a comment),
and missed that the real persistent stuck gate is :680. Line numbers drift on
the first nearby edit; a label name, a sentinel filename, a claim_page_once
flag or a shell function name does not. `marker` is a literal string the
validator locates in the source at runtime.
`sites` is the number of source sites this row is expected to cover, and it
is the load-bearing field. Without it a tenth dead end added directly beneath
an existing marker would INHERIT that marker and pass silently. With it, any
added or removed exit changes an observed count and the check goes RED.
Each row declares EXACTLY ONE of three dispositions:
consumer + liveness_check + reentry  -- a machine continues from here
terminal:true + rationale            -- an honest dead end, said out loud
error_path:true + error_evidence     -- reaching this state is a DEFECT and
the code says so loudly
A human is never a valid consumer -- the founder does not read or work on
code, so a state whose only actor is the founder does not continue.
`reentry` IS THE ANTI-FICTION FIELD (ASK-353). A liveness_check proves the
named job RAN. It cannot prove the job re-enters THIS state, and a job that
runs forever without ever selecting this state is a validator-satisfying
fiction -- the same shape as ci-redrive.py's false `it is also already
handled` comment, which cost 29 hours (ASK-352). So each consumer row names a
file and a literal marker inside that file, and the validator reads it: the
selector for this state must EXIST in the consumer's own source.

sources.what: Picks one ready issue and works it. Exits per issue via `continue` in the issue loop, via a ready() exclusion, or by applying a durable refusal label.
Drives ONE issue to a terminal PR state across up to MAX_ROUNDS rework rounds. It is a single-issue process, so every top-level exit ends that issue's run.
The launchd-driven selector. Every top-level exit ends a dispatch cycle, and an exit before the launch is a cycle in which no issue moved at all.

states.what: Sana refused the spec as unexecutable. The worker writes .sana-needs-scope, labels the issue needs-scope, and the picker stops offering it.
states.consumer: linear-dor-drafter.py -- selects on the needs-scope label, rewrites the DoR, drops the label so the picker offers it again

reentry.why: The drafter selects on the very label this state applies, so the selector for this state exists in the consumer's own source.

states.what: ready() excludes an issue with no Definition of Ready. It never entered a state; it was never picked.
states.consumer: linear-dor-drafter.py -- drafting a DoR for issues that lack one is the job this script exists for

reentry.why: The drafter writes the section whose absence is this state, so it demonstrably reads and resolves the condition.

states.what: rework_gate returned 10: approved, clean, pinned to its own head. Nothing to rework. The branch arms auto-merge and skips.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the next worker run re-evaluates this PR and re-arms; GitHub merges once required checks are green

reentry.why: The dispatcher's launch line re-runs converge on the issue, which re-runs the worker and re-evaluates this PR.

states.what: rework_gate returned 20: the PR has no recorded review verdict, so there is no spec to rework against.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- review-redrive.py offers the PR as a re-review pick and the dispatcher runs pr-review-agent.sh, which writes the verdict record this gate reads

reentry.marker: the reviewer has never posted a verdict for this PR
reentry.why: review-redrive.py's own selector for a PR with no verdict. Wired into the dispatcher at the REVIEW_REDRIVE call.

states.what: git worktree add failed and the tree still does not exist. Explicitly not counted against the issue.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the next run retries from scratch; nothing about the issue changed

reentry.why: The issue stays backlog/unstarted and ready, so the next dispatch launch re-selects it.

states.marker: skeleton guard set could not be built
states.what: The issue tree has no .claude/settings.json and skeleton-guard-settings.py could not build the guard set, so the worker refuses to start an unguarded agent and releases the claim. Explicitly not counted against the issue (ASK-3529).
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch: the next run rebuilds the set from the pinned skeleton, which advances to origin/main on each tick; nothing about the issue changed

reentry.why: The issue stays backlog/unstarted and ready, so the next dispatch launch re-selects it.

states.what: linear-claim.py exited 3: another session holds this worktree. A skip, not an error.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the holding session finishes and releases; the next run claims it. A claim left by a killed run is reclaimable on read via --holder-pid.

reentry.why: The issue is untouched and still ready, so the next dispatch launch re-selects it once the claim clears.

states.what: The claim failed for a reason that is not contention. Explicitly not counted against the issue.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- retried next run; a persistent failure surfaces through launchd-health-check.py, which pages on a job whose last run exited non-zero

reentry.why: Nothing about the issue changed, so the next dispatch launch re-selects it.

states.rationale: REFUSAL ON EVIDENCE, re-checked 2026-08-18 against the founder's reversal directive. The method this issue demands is: look for a successor that became real AFTER 2026-08-01, do not reason from the state name. Nothing did. Grepped the whole scripts tree for a reader of the blocked:capability label: linear-worker.sh applies it and counts it (held_with("blocked:capability")), and no other file selects on it. ASK-288 (`a blocked:capability label never expires, nothing re-tests the block`) is still open and is the named owner of the re-test, and this issue's Not-doing line excludes building it. The underlying reason is unchanged and is not a naming problem: the runner lacks something it cannot grant itself, and an agent must never grant itself an authorization (2026-05-17 scar). Revised to a consumer when ASK-288's re-test ships and is proven, not when it merges.

evidence.why: The only other reader of this label in the fleet is a COUNT in the same file that applies it. No selector re-enters the state.

states.what: An issue carrying owner:assaf. REVERSED 2026-08-03 by founder directive (`nothing should be on me`): this was a designed founder queue in the archived PRD prd-terminal-state-redrive-2026-08-01 and it is now a DEFECT. The queue was emptied this session (85 issues cleared) and by directive must never refill.
states.rationale: The v1 row read `this one is the intended destination, which is exactly why the rest must not quietly imitate it`. That reasoning was correct on 2026-08-01 and the founder has since closed the queue. A terminal:true row would keep certifying the routing as designed; an error_path row asserts the opposite -- that any issue reaching it is a bug the run has to say out loud. ready() still excludes the issue (the loop must not work something the founder marked hands-off, and silently working it would be worse), but the run now COUNTS and REPORTS the population and pages when it is non-zero, so a refilling queue is loud instead of invisible.

error_evidence.why: The loud refusal line the worker prints per run when the founder queue is non-empty. Absent from the source, this row is a claim with no code behind it.

states.what: The issue is not addressed to this worker.
states.rationale: Not an exit and not a refusal -- the issue was never routed here. A machine consumer would mean this worker picking up work nobody assigned to it, which is the opposite of what the ownership label is for. Board triage decides who owns an issue.

states.what: The issue is not in backlog or unstarted -- it is already started, done, or cancelled.
states.rationale: A correct exclusion, not a dead end. An issue in any other state either has an owner working it or is finished. Consuming this would mean re-opening closed work.

states.what: The issue is a ticket alert-to-linear.py filed, identified by the <!-- kipi-alert-fingerprint: ... --> marker the writer itself stamps.
states.rationale: A notification is not work, so refusing it here is the correct end and not a dead end. The body is a raw alert line, not a spec anyone scoped; drafting a DoR onto one would only make it READY-SHAPED and admit it to this queue. Measured on the live board 2026-08-15: 81 open alert tickets, and all 19 already drafted onto sat in the permanently-UNREACHABLE bucket. The consumer of an alert is the operator who reads it; the paired refusal in linear-dor-drafter.py stops the conversion at source. Registered with its own marker rather than left under state-not-open, whose row it would otherwise silently inflate to two sites -- which is exactly how this was caught.

states.what: The issue is ready-shaped and owned by Sana, but its Linear project is not this repo. 18 such issues across 14 projects as of 2026-08-01; one dispatch job exists fleet-wide.
states.rationale: NO CONSUMER TODAY. This is the largest parked population and it is deliberately left terminal rather than given a fake tier. Piece C (fleet-dispatch-preflight) is the named plan and it does not start until a per-repo preflight exists: a dispatcher that runs a client repo's local ./kipi, pushes branches and arms auto-merge is a real hazard to client_d and client_c, and opt-in plus a project filter is not protection (finding-8). Revised to a consumer when that preflight ships.

states.what: MAX_ATTEMPTS spent. One Linear comment (stuck_paged keeps it to one) names cap-ladder.py as the next step; no page.
states.consumer: cap-ladder.py -- reads the attempt count this branch tests and climbs one rung: RCA and continue, other runner, re-scope, a recorded decision

reentry.why: cap-ladder.py (ASK-3824) is the re-entrant driver this row lacked. Nightly it reads the persisted cap, has Fable write an RCA of the full packet, closes the capped PR with its branch kept, opens a new PR on the same branch, clears the record and requeues the ticket. Rung 2 runs the next attempt on the other runner, rung 3 re-scopes the DoR through linear-dor-drafter.py --issue, and rung 4 on is then a recorded decision: SPLIT into owned sub-tickets, CLOSE as Canceled with the RCA, or BLOCKED-ON an owned ticket or a fleet PR. A BLOCKED-ON ticket re-enters only on an event (its blocker closed, a touched file changed on main, its description changed, the model config changed), never on a timer. Founder 2026-11-08: 'What is gonna change in seven, fourteen or 28 days?'. The ladder's own per-issue rung count is the bound the ASK-830 scar asked for: the redrives still skip a capout until the ladder consumes it, and they never re-enter on their own. Founder 2026-11-08: a cap that ends in a park 'just hangs and goes nowhere'.

states.what: cap-ladder.py set ladder_hold: the RCA agent decided BLOCKED-ON an owned ticket or a fleet PR. The worker skips it before the dry pick.
states.consumer: cap-ladder.py -- clears the hold the night an event lands: the blocker closed, a file the last attempt touched or the RCA names changed on origin/main, the description changed, or the worker model config changed. No event, no run, one line naming what it waits on

reentry.why: The event check is the only thing that releases a hold. The blocker itself was validated as owned when the decision was written (check_blocker), and a blocker that later loses its owner is RED in the report, so a held ticket always waits on something that someone moves. Founder 2026-11-08: 'but what happens if nothing changed? the ticket just stays?'

states.marker: held while the second runner (Codex) is unavailable
states.what: Sana refused this issue on capability and Codex, the second runner, was out of credits or at its usage limit. The issue is held unlabelled and uncharged while the Codex outage claim is live, so no tick spends a paid Sana run on it only to reach the same dead Codex (PR #421 round 9). It records env_halt so converge charges and pages nothing.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the hold lifts when Codex answers for any issue (the outage claim is released) or the claim is older than CODEX_OUTAGE_MAX_AGE, and the next run dispatches the issue again

reentry.why: The issue keeps no label and no attempt charge, so the dispatcher re-selects it every tick; the worker releases the hold on its own once the claim is released or expired.

states.what: MAX_DRIFT_ROUNDS spent: the PR is approved at one sha but its head is still unreviewed. Paged once.
states.consumer: review-redrive.py -- classify() reads the verdict record's head_sha against the PR's live head and returns a re-review when they differ; kipi-dispatch.sh offers that pick ahead of a fresh issue and runs pr-review-agent.sh --post against the current head

reentry.why: The literal drift selector. THIS IS THE FOUNDER'S REVERSAL LANDING ON EVIDENCE, not a manufactured tier: the v1 row refused a review tier because a drift round already ends in a Codex review, which was true of a drift round INSIDE converge and said nothing about who re-enters the PR after the round budget is spent. review-redrive.py (ASK-352) landed 2026-08-03, after the PRD archived, and is exactly that missing re-entrant driver. Its cap is one attempt per PR per action per head sha, so it re-reviews the unreviewed head once rather than looping.

states.what: MAX_CONFLICT_ROUNDS spent: the PR is approved but still does not merge. One comment names cap-ladder.py; no page.
states.consumer: cap-ladder.py -- reads conflict_paged and moves the work to a new PR on the same branch after a fresh RCA

reentry.why: cap-ladder.py (ASK-3824) is the re-entrant driver this row lacked. Nightly it reads the persisted cap, has Fable write an RCA of the full packet, closes the capped PR with its branch kept, opens a new PR on the same branch, clears the record and requeues the ticket. A BLOCKED-ON ticket re-enters only on an event (its blocker closed, a touched file changed on main, its description changed, the model config changed), never on a timer. Founder 2026-11-08: 'What is gonna change in seven, fourteen or 28 days?'. The ladder's own per-issue rung count is the bound the ASK-830 scar asked for: the redrives still skip a capout until the ladder consumes it, and they never re-enter on their own. Founder 2026-11-08: a cap that ends in a park 'just hangs and goes nowhere'.

states.what: The worktree is missing the PR's commits and cannot be moved onto them because it holds local work. The round is refused rather than force-pushing over the approved diff. Paged once, and the claim is released so the issue is not wedged.
states.rationale: REFUSAL ON EVIDENCE, and the one state where a successor cannot become real by anyone shipping code. The PRD's own named example of an honest terminal. A tree holding local work has exactly two candidate machine moves -- discard the work, or force-push over a reviewed diff -- and both are on the destructive-op carve-out, which is hook-enforced and which an agent may not grant itself. A successor here would have to be a machine that decides what the founder's uncommitted work was for. The claim is already released so the issue is not wedged; a human decides.

evidence.why: The refusal itself. It releases the claim rather than resolving the tree, because both resolutions are destructive.

states.what: APPLY=0. The run reports what it would have done and counts the issue against LIMIT without touching it.
states.rationale: Not an issue state at all -- it is the caller's own --apply flag, and a live run never takes this branch. Registered rather than exempted because the enumerator finds every continue in the loop, and an exit that is genuinely not a dead end still has to be examined once and said out loud. Silence here would be indistinguishable from an unregistered exit.

states.what: An unrecognised flag, or no --issue at all. The run refuses before touching any issue.
states.rationale: No issue entered a state, so nothing is parked. The caller is a script or an operator typing the command, and the fix is the command line -- there is nothing persisted for a machine to re-enter. Registered rather than exempted for the same reason dry-run is: an exit that is genuinely not a dead end still has to be said out loud, because silence here is indistinguishable from an unregistered exit.

states.what: --dry. Reports the branch, PR and verdict it would work with, then stops.
states.rationale: The caller's own flag, exactly like the worker's dry-run row. A live dispatch never takes this branch, nothing is claimed and no state is written, so there is nothing for a consumer to continue from.

states.what: exit 8. The worker opened no PR AND the attempt could not be recorded, so the 3-attempt cap cannot trip and the issue would retry forever.
states.rationale: environmental-trigger, not latent-defect (self-healing-retry rule 5): the ledger file is unwritable -- a full disk, a permission change, a lock that never clears. Retrying cannot fix an environment, and a machine consumer here would be a loop re-entering the exact write that just failed while the cap it depends on is provably not enforceable. It pages once and stops, which is the correct behaviour for this class. There is deliberately no consumer.

evidence.marker: The 3-attempt cap keys on that file, so it cannot trip while the write fails
evidence.why: The exit exists precisely because the mechanism a retry would rely on is the thing that is broken.

states.marker: was NOT ATTEMPTED: the runner itself was unavailable
states.what: exit 9. The worker halted because the runner itself refused (a usage, session or weekly limit, 529 Overloaded, an auth failure) and recorded env_halt; converge charges no attempt and files no ticket.
states.rationale: environmental-trigger (self-healing-retry rule 5), and deliberately silent HERE because the worker already paged this outage once under its shared claim (env_alert_claim) and posted one Linear note on the halted issue. The exit-7 page this replaced filed one 'Sana could not open a PR' ticket per issue per tick for a single dead account (PR #421 round 1). The issue is not parked and nothing is charged, so the next dispatch after the runner recovers re-selects it; the consumer of the page is the worker's own emitter, not this exit.

states.marker: the usage breaker is holding this bot, so the round did no work by design
states.what: exit 3. The worker exited 3 because the usage breaker (ASK-2010) is holding this bot. It stopped before the fetch, the claim and the worktree, so the round did no work by design; converge charges no attempt and pages nobody.
states.rationale: A deliberate budget hold, not a failure, and silent HERE for the same reason as converge-env-halt: the breaker files its own single Linear ticket for Sana on the way into the pause and stays quiet while it holds, so a page from this exit would be one ticket per round for a condition already on the board. Before this branch existed a braked round fell through to the no-PR branch, charged an attempt and paged 'Sana could not open a PR'; three of those marked a healthy issue STUCK (claude review of PR #472, major 1). The issue is not parked and nothing is charged, so the next dispatch re-selects it once the breaker clears or grants its trial run.

evidence.why: The breaker lets one trial run through 24h after a pause and clears the pause itself once usage drops, so the hold ends without anyone acting.

states.what: exit 7. Sana ran and opened no PR on the branch. The attempt IS recorded, so this round is counted against the 3-attempt cap.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the issue is still backlog/unstarted and still ready, so the next dispatch cycle re-selects it and launches converge again, bounded by the attempts cap that the bump above just wrote

reentry.why: The dispatcher's launch line. Re-entry is bounded, not endless: the attempt was persisted before this exit, so the cap can trip, and when it does the issue lands in attempts-cap-stuck, which is registered terminal.

states.marker: but that verdict came from the DEGRADED Opus fallback
states.what: UNREACHABLE since ASK-3832. This was exit 7 on rework_gate returning 50 (a degraded approval). rework_gate no longer returns 50 for any input (test-degraded-approval-gate.sh case 5 sweeps all 525 combinations), so this branch cannot fire; a degraded approval now reaches converge-verdict-terminal like any approval.
states.rationale: Registered only because the dead branch is still in converge.sh source, and the validator enumerates exits from source. RULE-2026-11-06-C ruled that a degraded (Opus) approval is an approval and removed gate 50; ASK-3832 removed it from the lib and the worker. converge.sh was outside that PR's file list, so its branch stays until a converge.sh change deletes it together with this row. terminal:true is honest here: a branch no input reaches strands nothing.

states.what: exit 1. The PR reached a terminal verdict. The receipt is written, auto-merge state is reported, and the run is over.
states.rationale: REFUSAL ON EVIDENCE, and the refusal is about the INSTRUMENTS. This row used to read consumer: GitHub, with a launchd liveness_check on com.kipi.dispatch and a reentry marker inside converge.sh -- the driver that just exited. Neither field could be about GitHub: liveness_check has one kind, launchd, which reads a local plist and a local run-log, and reentry must name a file in this repo containing the selector. GitHub's merge daemon has neither, so the row was certified by probing a job it did not name and by pointing at code inside the exit itself. That is the validator-satisfying fiction this registry exists to refuse, reached from the inside (codex PR #215 round 4, major). What the exit reports: an approved PR whose record is not armed now gets armed by converge itself (ASK-310, automerge_arm); only gh REFUSING the arm, or answering neither arm nor state, pages -- in gh's own words, to Sana's Linear queue. The one page that still names a person and a command is an approved head NO prd-os receipt covers, armed or not: that page carries the receipt fix, not a merge command. The fourth hands off to GitHub, which does land it, and which no instrument here can certify; saying so is the honest answer, not naming it a consumer. The issue is DONE either way, which is why the class stays done: no kipi driver has more to do.

evidence.marker: approved but arming auto-merge was refused by gh
evidence.why: The exit's page text for the refused-arm sub-state (ASK-310). Before ASK-310 the unarmed sub-state paged 'Needs a human: gh pr merge'; converge now runs that arm itself, and what is left without a machine consumer is gh's refusal, which the page carries verbatim.

states.uncovered: A PR that is approved, green and armed and still does not land has NO consumer today, and neither does one whose arm gh refused (ASK-310 arms the unarmed case; a refusal pages Sana's queue with gh's reason). ci-redrive.py selects FAILED conclusions and review-redrive.py selects an absent, drifted or refused verdict; a green approved PR has neither. review-redrive.py's own header routes this case to ASK-310's pr-land-if-green.sh, which does not exist in this tree and is wired into neither driver. Tracked open at sp-9b01682d.

states.marker: review produced no verdict on round
states.what: exit 7 at gate 20. The review died or timed out, so there is no verdict record to rework against.
states.consumer: review-redrive.py -- a PR whose reviewer slot was never posted is its explicit first-re-review case; the dispatcher runs pr-review-agent.sh --post against it ahead of a fresh pick

reentry.marker: the reviewer has never posted a verdict for this PR
reentry.why: The literal selector for a PR with no verdict, in the consumer's own source. Same code path the worker-side no-review-verdict row names, reached from the other driver.

states.what: exit 5. The round changed no code AND drew the same verdict, so another round would re-read the same review and produce the same nothing.
states.rationale: REFUSAL ON EVIDENCE. The two ways out are both already spent by construction: re-reviewing is what review-redrive.py does and its cap is one attempt per PR per action per head sha -- and this exit fires only when the head did NOT move, so that cap is either spent or about to be, and re-offering cannot produce a different answer. Reworking is what just ran and changed nothing. A consumer here is the manufactured tier the archived PRD named and dropped: it would re-enter the identical inputs forever and write a Linear comment on every round. The gate-40 variant of the page states the specific unreviewed-head case so the operator is not told a benign stall.

evidence.marker: Requiring BOTH avoids a false stop
evidence.why: The exit already requires same-verdict AND same-sha, which is exactly the input a redrive would re-enter with.

states.what: exit 2. MAX_ROUNDS spent without a terminal verdict. The cap-out is written to the attempts ledger; the redrives skip it and cap-ladder.py consumes it.
states.consumer: cap-ladder.py -- reads the capout record, writes an RCA, opens a new PR on the same branch and clears the record

reentry.why: cap-ladder.py (ASK-3824) is the re-entrant driver this row lacked. Nightly it reads the persisted cap, has Fable write an RCA of the full packet, closes the capped PR with its branch kept, opens a new PR on the same branch, clears the record and requeues the ticket. Rung 2 runs the next attempt on the other runner, rung 3 re-scopes the DoR through linear-dor-drafter.py --issue, and rung 4 on is then a recorded decision: SPLIT into owned sub-tickets, CLOSE as Canceled with the RCA, or BLOCKED-ON an owned ticket or a fleet PR. A BLOCKED-ON ticket re-enters only on an event (its blocker closed, a touched file changed on main, its description changed, the model config changed), never on a timer. Founder 2026-11-08: 'What is gonna change in seven, fourteen or 28 days?'. The ladder's own per-issue rung count is the bound the ASK-830 scar asked for: the redrives still skip a capout until the ladder consumes it, and they never re-enter on their own. Founder 2026-11-08: a cap that ends in a park 'just hangs and goes nowhere'.

states.what: exit 143/130/129. TERM, INT or HUP arrived mid-run. The trap releases the claim this run left on the issue and ends the process, abandoning the round in flight. Registered only after the enumerator learned to walk trap handlers (codex PR #215 round 3): a handler has no top-level call site, so the function-body exclusion hid it and this exit was invisible to every check in the suite.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the trap releases the claim BEFORE exiting, so the issue is left unclaimed, still backlog/unstarted and still ready, and the next dispatch cycle re-selects it and launches converge again

reentry.why: The dispatcher's launch line -- the same re-entry converge-no-pr-opened names, and it is reached here for the same reason: a released claim puts the issue back in the ready pool. UNLIKE that row, re-entry here is NOT bounded by the attempts cap. The signal arrives before the ledger bump, so no attempt is recorded and the round is free. That is right for an operator pressing Ctrl-C and wrong if something starts killing converge on a clock: nothing in this tree does today (no timeout wraps the launch in kipi-dispatch.sh), and the residual is captured in the spillover ledger rather than dressed up as bounded here.

states.what: The dispatcher cannot cd into $REPO. The whole Linear loop is dead, not slow.
states.rationale: environmental-trigger. The path in com.kipi.dispatch.plist is wrong or the checkout is gone; no amount of re-running reaches a repo that is not there, and the only actor who can restore it is outside this machine's control loop. It pages once via page_once, which is the correct behaviour for this class.

states.what: This checkout is behind origin/main, so dispatching would run superseded control code. The cycle stops.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the next tick re-runs stale_check, and the moment the checkout is fast-forwarded the same guard passes and page_clear turns the recovery into silence

reentry.why: The guard is re-evaluated on every tick of the same job, so the state is re-entered by construction rather than by a separate selector.

states.what: MAX_CONCURRENT converge runs are already live. The cycle yields rather than adding another.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the next tick re-counts live converges and dispatches as soon as one finishes

reentry.why: The count is recomputed every tick, so the condition clears on its own as the live runs end.

states.what: Neither BSD nor GNU date could compute the budget window, so the dispatcher refuses to run uncapped.
states.rationale: environmental-trigger, and the refusal is the point. The spend cap is derived from this value; without it the loop would dispatch with no daily bound, which is the one failure mode that costs real money unattended. A consumer would be a retry of the same date call in the same environment. It pages once and stops.

states.what: KIPI_DISPATCH_LANE is set to something other than production or test, so the spend counter and lane cap cannot be resolved.
states.rationale: A misconfigured environment variable in the caller, not an issue state. No issue was selected and nothing is parked. Refusing loudly is correct: guessing a lane would pick a budget counter at random, and the production one is the unattended self-merging path.

states.what: DAILY_MAX issues already dispatched for this budget day. The loop rests until the reset hour.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the budget day rolls at RESET_HOUR and the next tick after that computes a new BUDGET_DAY, a fresh counter file, and dispatches again

reentry.why: The counter is keyed on a day that advances on its own, so the cap clears without anyone acting. The paged sentinel exists only to page once, not per tick.

states.marker: memory gate: not filling a slot this tick
states.what: The Mac is short of memory (the system memory-free percentage under its floor, or the claude processes at their ceiling), so the pass starts no new converge (ASK-4008). Added after 2026-11-08, when about 16 parallel claude processes pushed swap to about 10 GB and filled the disk.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the next tick reads memory again; when runs finish and memory frees, the same read passes and page_clear turns the recovery into silence

reentry.why: Memory is read again on every tick of the same job, and it frees by itself as runs finish, so the state clears without anyone acting.

states.what: The gh CLI is not on PATH and was not found in the usual install dirs, so no PR can be opened.
states.rationale: environmental-trigger: a missing binary. The loop cannot install its own tooling, and retrying a PATH lookup that just failed is the definition of a fake tier. It pages once; the healthy path calls page_clear so a recovery is silent and the next episode pages immediately.

states.what: Free disk is under the worktree floor (refuse_worktree_below_gb) even after one worktree-reaper pass, so the tick dispatches nothing, claims nothing and spends no budget (ASK-3648). It pages once per episode as a notice, because a full disk stops the whole fleet.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- every tick measures again, runs worktree-reaper.py --apply, and dispatches as soon as free space is back over the floor

reentry.why: The floor is measured at the top of every tick of the same job, before the turn lock. Nothing about the issue changed, so nothing is charged; the tick that finds space dispatches normally.

states.marker: another dispatcher holds the selection turn
states.what: Another dispatcher is mid read-select-advance. This one yields rather than racing the cursor.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the holder finishes and advances the cursor, and the next tick takes the lock

reentry.why: The lock is re-attempted every tick of the same job. Explicitly not an error: the other dispatcher is doing the work this one skipped.

states.what: KIPI_DISPATCH_PICK_DRY=1. Prints the picks the real path would take and exits before anything is claimed.
states.rationale: The caller's own flag, like the two other dry-run rows in this registry. A live launchd run never sets it, nothing is claimed and no agent starts, so there is no state for a consumer to continue from. It runs after the preflight filter on purpose so the report does not lie in the safe-looking direction.

states.what: The rotation produced no repo the preflight will accept this turn.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the rotation cursor advances, so the next tick starts from a different position and reaches a different repo

reentry.why: The selection re-runs from an advanced cursor every tick. A repo the preflight permanently refuses is reported by the worker's own REFUSED bucket, not silently parked here.

states.marker: its registry path contains whitespace or a glob character
states.what: The chosen repo's instance-registry path holds whitespace or a glob character, which cannot be passed safely as an unquoted word.
states.rationale: A loud refusal beating a silent wrong target: this decides which repository an unattended self-merging loop enters, and a mis-expanded path could enter the wrong one. The fix is the registry row, which a machine must not rewrite on its own -- editing the path a dispatcher will `cd` into is exactly the class of change that needs a human. Caught on PR #146 (sp-b2f0627e); the glob half was missed on the first cut.

states.what: kipi work reported Linear unreachable or auth expired, so NO issue can be picked. The loop is stopped, not slow.
states.rationale: environmental-trigger (self-healing-retry rule 5): an unreachable service or an expired credential. Retrying logic cannot fix an environment, and an expired token is an authorization an agent must never renew for itself. page_once means one page per episode, and the healthy path clears it so a recovery is silent.

states.what: The worker stopped on a git fetch failure BEFORE reaching Linear. The dispatcher exits without paging and without clearing the linear-down state.
states.rationale: environmental-trigger, and deliberately silent HERE because the worker already pages this one itself -- double-paging one failure is how an operator learns to skim. The rule it enforces is that a run which never reached Linear is not evidence Linear recovered. The consumer of the page is the worker's own emitter, not this exit.

states.marker: worker is BRAKED by the usage breaker
states.what: exit 0. The worker exited 3 because the usage breaker (ASK-2010) is holding the bot. It stopped before reaching Linear, so the dispatcher exits without paging and without clearing the linear-down state.
states.rationale: A deliberate budget hold, and silent HERE because the breaker files its own single Linear ticket on the way into the pause; paging would be one ticket per 15-minute beat for a condition already on the board. Keyed on the exit code, not the message, and kept separate from dispatch-worker-infra-stop: a braked run never reached Linear, so it is no more evidence that Linear recovered than a failed fetch is, and clearing linear-down on it would erase the state that pages a real outage (claude review of PR #472, major 2).

evidence.why: The breaker lets one trial run through 24h after a pause and clears the pause itself once usage drops, so the hold ends without anyone acting.

states.what: No fresh pick and no redrive candidate. There is simply nothing to dispatch.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the next tick re-queries the board, and any issue that becomes ready (a DoR drafted, a label dropped, a new issue filed) is picked then

reentry.why: An empty queue re-fills from outside; the selection re-runs every tick. This is the honest empty-board case, not a park.

states.marker: a converge run for it is already live
states.what: A converge process for the chosen issue is already in the process table. The cycle skips rather than starting a second one.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the live run is the consumer; when it ends, its own exit is a registered converge state and the next tick re-selects if the issue is still ready

reentry.why: The snapshot is retaken every tick, so the skip lasts exactly as long as the live run. The work is not parked; it is already happening.

states.what: branch_guard (ASK-358) refused this dispatch: the issue's open PR is on a branch converge would not commit into, or the issue maps to more than one live branch. The refusing tick spends a redrive's attempt at that head (mark-dispatched) and sets the issue aside for a day in ~/.config/kipi/dispatch-branch-refused.tsv, then exits 0 (ASK-3993).
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the next tick passes the set-aside list to the worker as KIPI_PICK_EXCLUDE and the spent attempt keeps the redrive selector off that PR head, so the queue moves past the issue; after a day the list drops it and the guard re-tests it, where a closed or renamed PR passes and page_clear turns the recovery into silence. This replaces the OPERATOR-BLOCKED reading of PR #266 round 1: the condition still needs the branch owner, but the queue no longer waits on it, and the PR itself is carried by the open-pr board state (wip_release, ASK-3962).

reentry.why: Every tick hands the day's set-aside list to the worker pick, so a refused issue is left out until its day ends and is then offered to the guard again.

states.what: The red-CI redrive attempt for this issue was already claimed (or the ledger could not be written, which is the same answer -- nothing was recorded, so nothing may act as though it was).
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- whoever holds the claim is dispatching it; ci-redrive.py re-offers the PR on a new failure signature, and the next tick picks it up

reentry.why: The redrive is re-consulted every tick and its cap is per PR per failure signature, so a genuinely new red re-offers the same PR.

states.what: The reviewer-redrive attempt for this issue and PR was already claimed at this head sha.
states.consumer: com.kipi.dispatch -- the claim holder is dispatching it; review-redrive.py re-offers the PR when the head moves, and the next tick picks it up

reentry.why: The redrive is re-consulted every tick and its cap keys on the head sha, so a moved head re-offers the same PR.

states.what: The converge launch returned non-zero. The budget slot is already spent and no work is happening even though the loop looks alive.
states.rationale: environmental-trigger: the process could not be started at all (a missing interpreter, an exhausted fork/file limit, a broken ./kipi). The budget slot is spent, so a silent retry would burn the day's cap on a launch that keeps failing for a reason outside the loop. It pages with the reproduce command rather than looping. The issue itself is not parked: it stays ready and a later tick re-selects it once the machine is healthy.

states.what: The tail of the dispatch confirmation block, both arms: exit 1 when the launched converge is gone after 10s, and the final exit 0 when it is confirmed running. Registered as one row because the two arms sit inside one if/else with nothing between them a marker could anchor to -- claiming otherwise would be a marker inventing a boundary the source does not have.
states.rationale: The failing arm is environmental-trigger: the process launched and died immediately, which is a broken interpreter or a crashing ./kipi, and the budget slot is already spent -- so a retry tier would burn the daily cap on a process that cannot stay up. It pages with the log path. The succeeding arm is not a dead end at all: the converge run IS the consumer and its own exits are registered under the converge source above. Both are honest ends of this driver's cycle, which is why one rationale covers the pair.

_doc: ONE ROW PER HOLD KIND AT THE WIP CEILING (ASK-3866, RULE-2026-11-07-A).
At 5 open fleet-own PRs the worker stops starting issues (ASK-3826). On
2026-11-07 8 PRs no worker round could move held that ceiling, and every
tick started nothing. So every tick at the ceiling now releases ONE passed-
over PR, oldest first, through the exit its hold kind names here.
A kind is the machine key the picker (hold(...) in linear-worker.sh) or
wip_move_why (printf '<kind>|...') emits. Exits:
close-requeue  close the PR with its last FINDINGS block, keep the branch,
ticket back to Backlog with resume-from-branch, one attempt
close-comment  close the PR, keep the branch, one comment on the ticket
wait           a named consumer with an expiry owns it; the backstop takes
the oldest past the age bar unless backstop is false
A release never deletes a branch and never touches a review record, so a
PR keeps its own round count; reopening it undoes the release.
A kind with no row is read as wait with backstop true, and
test-worker-wip-liveness.sh L11 fails while any emitted kind has no row,
or any row names no emitted kind.

cap.what: At the reviewer round cap: a push gets no new review. ASK-3824 takes the cap sites over when it lands, and its last step still closes the PR and requeues the ticket.
cap.consumer: linear-worker.sh wip_release (ASK-3866), this table's one reader; kipi-dispatch.sh applies it (WIP-RELEASE-APPLY). The ticket returns to Backlog through linear-sync.py requeue, and the worker picks it up again; one attempt is charged, so MAX_ATTEMPTS bounds it.

attempts.what: The ticket spent MAX_ATTEMPTS worker attempts.
attempts.consumer: linear-worker.sh wip_release (ASK-3866), this table's one reader; kipi-dispatch.sh applies it (WIP-RELEASE-APPLY). The ticket returns to Backlog through linear-sync.py requeue, and the worker picks it up again; one attempt is charged, so MAX_ATTEMPTS bounds it.

conflict.what: Still conflicting after MAX_CONFLICT_ROUNDS rebase rounds.
conflict.consumer: linear-worker.sh wip_release (ASK-3866), this table's one reader; kipi-dispatch.sh applies it (WIP-RELEASE-APPLY). The ticket returns to Backlog through linear-sync.py requeue, and the worker picks it up again; one attempt is charged, so MAX_ATTEMPTS bounds it.

drift.what: Head still unreviewed after MAX_DRIFT_ROUNDS drift rounds.
drift.consumer: linear-worker.sh wip_release (ASK-3866), this table's one reader; kipi-dispatch.sh applies it (WIP-RELEASE-APPLY). The ticket returns to Backlog through linear-sync.py requeue, and the worker picks it up again; one attempt is charged, so MAX_ATTEMPTS bounds it.

lane.what: A lane branch sana/<id>-<slug> the worker cannot rework, its ticket not live. Adoption onto sana/<id> with the round count carried is ASK-3938.
lane.consumer: linear-worker.sh wip_release (ASK-3866), this table's one reader; kipi-dispatch.sh applies it (WIP-RELEASE-APPLY). The ticket returns to Backlog through linear-sync.py requeue, and the worker picks it up again; one attempt is charged, so MAX_ATTEMPTS bounds it.

alert.what: The ticket is a fleet alert (ASK-839), not dispatch work.
alert.consumer: linear-worker.sh wip_release (ASK-3866), this table's one reader; kipi-dispatch.sh applies it (WIP-RELEASE-APPLY). The ticket itself belongs to linear-alert-triage.py.

refused-label.what: The ticket carries owner:assaf, needs-scope or blocked:capability, or lacks owner:sana.
refused-label.consumer: linear-worker.sh wip_release (ASK-3866), this table's one reader; kipi-dispatch.sh applies it (WIP-RELEASE-APPLY). The label has its own consumer: linear-dor-drafter.py for needs-scope, the capability grant for blocked:capability.

no-dor.what: The ticket has no Definition of Ready.
no-dor.consumer: linear-worker.sh wip_release (ASK-3866), this table's one reader; kipi-dispatch.sh applies it (WIP-RELEASE-APPLY). linear-dor-drafter.py drafts the DoR; the worker picks the ticket again once it has one.

off-repo.what: The ticket is on another project, so this repo worker never picks it.
off-repo.consumer: linear-worker.sh wip_release (ASK-3866), this table's one reader; kipi-dispatch.sh applies it (WIP-RELEASE-APPLY). That project worker owns the ticket.

ticket-closed.what: The ticket is Done or Canceled; the PR outlived it.
ticket-closed.consumer: linear-worker.sh wip_release (ASK-3866), this table's one reader; kipi-dispatch.sh applies it (WIP-RELEASE-APPLY). Nothing more: the ticket is closed and is not requeued.

not-on-board.what: The branch names a ticket that is not on the board.
not-on-board.consumer: linear-worker.sh wip_release (ASK-3866), this table's one reader; kipi-dispatch.sh applies it (WIP-RELEASE-APPLY). Nothing more: there is no ticket to requeue.

approved.what: Approved at its head; it waits on a merge or on CI.
approved.consumer: Auto-merge on a green head; ci-redrive.py (ASK-295) on a red one; the backstop past the age bar.

unreviewed.consumer: review-redrive.py runs the reviewer; the backstop past the age bar.

codex.what: Held while the second runner (Codex) is unavailable.
codex.consumer: The Codex outage claim, released when Codex answers or at CODEX_OUTAGE_MAX_AGE (a day).

ticket-held.what: A started ticket held by the ASK-3825 rule for a reason other than a live run.
ticket-held.consumer: linear-sync.py started_hold_reason releases it when its hold ends; the backstop past the age bar.

ticket-live.what: A started ticket inside the lane window or under a live worker claim: someone may be on it now.
ticket-live.consumer: The 24h lane window (linear-sync.py STARTED_STALE_HOURS) or the claim ends, and the PR is judged again. Never the backstop: closing it would throw away a live round.

lane-live.what: A lane branch whose ticket is inside the lane window or under a live claim.
lane-live.consumer: The 24h lane window ends, then kind lane and its exit. Never the backstop: a supervised lane may be on it.

ticket-state.what: The ticket is in a state the picker does not take (for example Triage).
ticket-state.consumer: Linear triage moves it; the backstop past the age bar.

set-aside.what: Its ticket was set aside for a day after a dispatcher branch refusal (ASK-3993): reworking it would only be refused again.
set-aside.consumer: kipi-dispatch.sh BRANCH REFUSAL EXIT: the set-aside row expires after a day and the guard re-tests the ticket; the backstop past the age bar.

walk.what: Past the walk bound of 10 candidates, so not checked this tick.
walk.consumer: Transient: the walk reaches it as older PRs leave; the backstop past the age bar.

_doc: RULE-2026-11-07-B. One row per state a TICKET or PR can sit in on the board, with a max age
and the exits that take it out. Read by test-fleet-liveness.py (coverage and bounds, in CI)
and by fleet-health-daily.py detector liveness-debt-expired (the dates, daily, with a real clock).
An exit is a consumer or a debt. A consumer names a file, a literal marker the test finds in
it, and the test that proves it fires. `fires: by-age` means the code takes the item out by
age; `by-order` means it drains the state in some order with no age guarantee. A state is
live only if it has a by-age consumer or an open debt. A debt names the ticket that builds
the by-age exit, and expires at most 30 days after `since`: a debt is a dated promise, never
a permanent excuse (P5 in stuck-work-synthesis-2026-11-07.md: a written reason in place of
a coded exit is how every half-port passed the last check).
`covers` lists the `states` rows (the per-site registry above) this board state holds
tickets for. Every `states` row of a ticket-holding class must be covered, or listed in
`not_a_state` with its reason, so a new stop added to a driver fails CI until it has a row.

not_a_state.dispatch-daily-cap: A rate, not a state: no ticket is held by it, the next budget day takes the same picks.
not_a_state.dispatch-memory-gate: A rate, not a state: no ticket is held by it, the next tick with room takes the same picks.

needs-triage-alert.what: An alert ticket labelled needs-triage, waiting for the triage lane.

exits.what: Decides promote or close, oldest first, a fixed number a night (D1).
chief's triage parks an idle Backlog ticket after 30 days and chief #370 (ASK-3955) closes it, reversibly, at the review date; recorded here once the table can name a cross-repo consumer.

no-project.what: A ready-shaped ticket with no Linear project or no owner label, so no worker owns it.

exits.what: Nightly through linear-triage-health.py (09:00, 10 writes a run): a no-project ticket with path or title-label evidence gets its project, DoR or not (ASK-3959 stage 1). Measured 2026-11-08: 73 of 384 route.

Nightly (com.kipi.linear-route-decide, 05:20, 20 a night): what no rule routes gets one validated decision, ROUTE to a dispatch target on the board, CLOSE (Canceled with the reason, reversible) or SPLIT (a route to its first part, the parts in the record, no ticket filed). A write that was undone is never made again; a reopened close is routed instead (ASK-4133). Two refused answers land on CLOSE, no fleet repo owns this. No park (ASK-3959 stage 2). Measured 2026-11-09: 350 tickets in its population.

no-checkout.what: A ticket whose project names a repo with no local checkout the dispatcher can enter.

exits.what: E7: auto-clone a registry row with a pinned remote; else park dispatch-off.

repo-refused.what: A ticket in a repo whose latest preflight refuses it (the 240 of 11-07).

exits.what: E6: the 2nd refusal of one check parks the repo's tickets repo-refused.
E8: the nightly probe re-test clears the label when the probe passes.

attempts-exhausted.what: A ticket whose 3 worker attempts are spent, or whose PR is capped (rounds, review rounds, rebase rounds, the review-redrive machine tier).

exits.what: Nightly, one rung per cap: RCA and continue, other runner, re-scope, then one recorded decision (SPLIT, CLOSE or BLOCKED-ON an owned blocker). A held ticket re-enters on an event, never a timer (ASK-3824).

ready-over-cap.what: A ready ticket behind more than 2 weeks of merges (215 ready at about 2.4 merges a day).

exits.what: NEW-6 parks the overflow icebox, paired with ASK-3955's 30-day close (D13).

started-dormant.what: A started ticket nobody is working: no live claim, no open PR, started over 24 hours ago.

exits.what: ready() offers it again once started_hold_reason is empty (ASK-3825).

owner-assaf.what: A ticket labelled owner:assaf; the founder has said he will not act on these.

exits.what: E10: relabel owner:sana unless it asks a spend, scope or reach question.

needs-scope.what: A ticket with no Definition of Ready, or one the worker refused as unexecutable.

exits.what: The nightly drafter writes or rewrites the DoR, up to 3 redrafts.
chief's triage parks an idle Backlog ticket after 30 days and chief #370 (ASK-3955) closes it, reversibly, at the review date; recorded here once the table can name a cross-repo consumer.

open-pr.what: An open fleet PR held by a cap, a refused branch, or a stalled converge.

exits.what: At the WIP ceiling each tick releases one PR no round can move (RULE-2026-11-07-A).
com.kipi.pr-owner, hourly: every open PR in a dispatch repo, any branch, below the ceiling too. At 48h old and 12h quiet it merges, reviews, reworks once, or closes with the branch kept (ASK-3962).

consumer-report.what: A consumer's own report: in and done per run, read off the Mac (missing past 2 periods, or starved twice).

exits.what: heartbeat.yml opens a heartbeat-red issue when a row is 2 periods old or starved twice; fleet-health mirrors it into Linear (ASK-3947).
